tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>

Le port 5432 est exposé, les données sont gardées dans un volume nommé `pgdata`, et un healthcheck `pg_isready` vérifie que la base répond. `docker compose config` accepte le fichier, mais je n'ai pas lancé le conteneur.

J'ai aussi ajouté deux lignes dans `README.md` pour expliquer comment s'en servir : `docker compose up -d`, puis `DATABASE_URL=postgresql+psycopg://cayzn:cayzn@localhost:5432/cayzn`.

**À faire avant que ça marche :** aucun driver Postgres n'est installé dans le projet, donc cette URL échouera tant que tu n'as pas lancé `uv add "psycopg[binary]"`. Je ne l'ai pas ajouté moi-même parce que tu ne l'avais pas demandé ; dis-moi si tu veux que je le fasse.

Je n'ai pas mis l'app elle-même dans le compose : tu la lances déjà en local avec `fastapi dev`.

La connexion à la base passe maintenant par pydantic-settings, dans `src/cayzn/db.py`. Une classe `Settings` lit `DATABASE_URL` depuis l'environnement ou depuis un fichier `.env`, avec toujours `sqlite:///./cayzn.db` par défaut. `pydantic-settings` est ajouté aux dépendances (`pyproject.toml` et `uv.lock`), et la ligne du README sur `DATABASE_URL` mentionne le `.env`.

Le test passe, tous les contrôles de pre-commit (ruff, ty, uv-lock) aussi, et j'ai vérifié qu'une valeur de `DATABASE_URL` passée par l'environnement est bien prise en compte. `just` n'est pas installé sur ta machine, donc j'ai lancé directement les commandes de `just test` et `just check`.

Pour Postgres, il manque toujours le driver : `uv add "psycopg[binary]"`. Ensuite, mets `DATABASE_URL=postgresql+psycopg://cayzn:cayzn@localhost:5432/cayzn` dans `.env` (le fichier est déjà dans `.gitignore`).

J'ai gardé `Settings` dans `db.py` puisqu'il n'y a qu'un seul réglage pour l'instant. On pourra le sortir dans un `config.py` quand d'autres réglages arriveront.

+from logging.config import fileConfig
+
+from alembic import context
+from sqlalchemy import engine_from_config, pool
+
+from cayzn import models  # noqa: F401  (enregistre les tables)
+from cayzn.db import Base, settings
+
+# this is the Alembic Config object, which provides
+# access to the values within the .ini file in use.
+config = context.config
+
+# Interpret the config file for Python logging.
+# This line sets up loggers basically.
+if config.config_file_name is not None:
+    fileConfig(config.config_file_name)
+
+# % échappé : la config Alembic interpole les valeurs (mots de passe encodés).
+config.set_main_option("sqlalchemy.url", str(settings.database_url).replace("%", "%%"))
+target_metadata = Base.metadata
+
+# other values from the config, defined by the needs of env.py,
+# can be acquired:
+# my_important_option = config.get_main_option("my_important_option")
+# ... etc.
+
+
+def run_migrations_offline() -> None:
+    """Run migrations in 'offline' mode.
+
+    This configures the context with just a URL
+    and not an Engine, though an Engine is acceptable
+    here as well.  By skipping the Engine creation
+    we don't even need a DBAPI to be available.
+
+    Calls to context.execute() here emit the given string to the
+    script output.
+
+    """
+    url = config.get_main_option("sqlalchemy.url")
+    context.configure(
+        url=url,
+        target_metadata=target_metadata,
+        render_as_batch=True,
+        literal_binds=True,
+        dialect_opts={"paramstyle": "named"},
+    )
+
+    with context.begin_transaction():
+        context.run_migrations()
+
+
+def run_migrations_online() -> None:
+    """Run migrations in 'online' mode.
+
+    In this scenario we need to create an Engine
+    and associate a connection with the context.
+
+    """
+    connectable = engine_from_config(
+        config.get_section(config.config_ini_section, {}),
+        prefix="sqlalchemy.",
+        poolclass=pool.NullPool,
+    )
+
+    with connectable.connect() as connection:
+        context.configure(
+            connection=connection,
+            target_metadata=target_metadata,
+            render_as_batch=True,  # ALTER TABLE sous SQLite
+        )
+
+        with context.begin_transaction():
+            context.run_migrations()
+
+
+if context.is_offline_mode():
+    run_migrations_offline()
+else:
+    run_migrations_online()

+"""Import nocturne du plan de transport depuis les CSV du système de réservation.
+
+Usage : python -m cayzn.importer <dossier>  (trains.csv, stops.csv, ods.csv, prices.csv)
+
+L'import est idempotent : relancé sur les mêmes fichiers, il ne change rien.
+Tout est fait dans une seule transaction : une ligne invalide annule l'import entier.
+"""
+
+import csv
+import sys
+from collections.abc import Iterator
+from datetime import date
+from decimal import Decimal, InvalidOperation
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from sqlalchemy import select
+from sqlalchemy.orm import Session, selectinload
+
+from cayzn.db import SessionLocal
+from cayzn.models import OriginDestination, Service, ServiceStop, Stop
+
+ServiceKey = tuple[str, date]
+
+
+class TransportPlanError(ValueError):
+    pass
+
+
+def _rows(path: Path, columns: set[str]) -> Iterator[tuple[str, dict[str, str]]]:
+    """Lignes du CSV avec leur emplacement `fichier:ligne` pour les messages d'erreur."""
+    with path.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
+        reader = csv.DictReader(f)
+        missing = columns - set(reader.fieldnames or [])
+        if missing:
+            raise TransportPlanError(
+                f"{path.name}: colonnes manquantes {sorted(missing)}"
+            )
+        for row in reader:
+            where = f"{path.name}:{reader.line_num}"
+            if any(not (row[c] or "").strip() for c in columns):
+                raise TransportPlanError(f"{where}: valeur vide")
+            yield where, {c: row[c].strip() for c in columns}
+
+
+def _service_key(where: str, row: dict[str, str]) -> ServiceKey:
+    try:
+        return row["name"], date.fromisoformat(row["departure_date"])
+    except ValueError:
+        raise TransportPlanError(
+            f"{where}: date invalide {row['departure_date']!r}"
+        ) from None
+
+
+def import_transport_plan(session: Session, directory: Path) -> None:
+    keys = [
+        _service_key(where, row)
+        for where, row in _rows(directory / "trains.csv", {"departure_date", "name"})
+    ]
+
+    # Précharge l'existant pour éviter une requête par ligne.
+    existing = session.scalars(
+        select(Service)
+        .where(Service.departure_date.in_({d for _, d in keys}))
+        .options(selectinload(Service.stops), selectinload(Service.ods))
+    )
+    services: dict[ServiceKey, Service] = {
+        (s.name, s.departure_date): s for s in existing
+    }
+    for name, departure_date in keys:
+        if (name, departure_date) not in services:
+            services[name, departure_date] = Service(
+                name=name, departure_date=departure_date
+            )
+            session.add(services[name, departure_date])
+    services = {key: services[key] for key in keys}
+
+    stops = {s.code: s for s in session.scalars(select(Stop))}
+
+    def stop(code: str) -> Stop:
+        if code not in stops:
+            stops[code] = Stop(code=code)
+            session.add(stops[code])
+        return stops[code]
+
+    def service(where: str, row: dict[str, str]) -> Service:
+        key = _service_key(where, row)
+        if key not in services:
+            raise TransportPlanError(
+                f"{where}: service {key[0]} du {key[1]} absent de trains.csv"
+            )
+        return services[key]
+
+    # Itinéraires : l'ordre des lignes de stops.csv donne l'ordre de desserte.
+    itineraries: dict[ServiceKey, list[str]] = {}
+    for where, row in _rows(
+        directory / "stops.csv", {"departure_date", "name", "stops"}
+    ):
+        codes = itineraries.setdefault(_service_key(where, row), [])
+        service(where, row)
+        if row["stops"] in codes:
+            raise TransportPlanError(f"{where}: arrêt {row['stops']} en double")
+        codes.append(row["stops"])
+
+    for key, codes in itineraries.items():
+        svc = services[key]
+        if [s.stop.code for s in svc.stops] == codes:
+            continue
+        svc.stops.clear()
+        session.flush()  # supprime l'ancien itinéraire avant de réinsérer les mêmes clés
+        svc.stops.extend(
+            ServiceStop(position=i, stop=stop(c)) for i, c in enumerate(codes)
+        )
+
+    def od_key(od: OriginDestination) -> tuple[str, str]:
+        return od.origin.code, od.destination.code
+
+    ods = {(id(svc), *od_key(od)): od for svc in services.values() for od in svc.ods}
+
+    def find_od(
+        where: str, row: dict[str, str]
+    ) -> tuple[Service, OriginDestination | None]:
+        svc = service(where, row)
+        return svc, ods.get((id(svc), row["origin"], row["destination"]))
+
+    for where, row in _rows(
+        directory / "ods.csv", {"departure_date", "name", "origin", "destination"}
+    ):
+        svc, od = find_od(where, row)
+        if od:
+            continue
+        positions = {s.stop.code: s.position for s in svc.stops}
+        o, d = row["origin"], row["destination"]
+        if o not in positions or d not in positions:
+            raise TransportPlanError(
+                f"{where}: {o}-{d} n'est pas desservi par le service {svc.name}"
+            )
+        if positions[o] >= positions[d]:
+            raise TransportPlanError(
+                f"{where}: {o} n'est pas avant {d} dans l'itinéraire"
+            )
+        od = OriginDestination(origin=stop(o), destination=stop(d))
+        svc.ods.append(od)
+        ods[(id(svc), o, d)] = od
+
+    for where, row in _rows(
+        directory / "prices.csv",
+        {"departure_date", "name", "origin", "destination", "price"},
+    ):
+        _, od = find_od(where, row)
+        if od is None:
+            raise TransportPlanError(
+                f"{where}: OD {row['origin']}-{row['destination']} absente de ods.csv"
+            )
+        try:
+            price = Decimal(row["price"])
+        except InvalidOperation:
+            raise TransportPlanError(
+                f"{where}: prix invalide {row['price']!r}"
+            ) from None
+        if not price.is_finite() or price < 0:
+            raise TransportPlanError(f"{where}: prix invalide {row['price']!r}")
+        od.price = price
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    if len(sys.argv) != 2:
+        sys.exit("usage: python -m cayzn.importer <dossier>")
+    with SessionLocal.begin() as session:
+        import_transport_plan(session, Path(sys.argv[1]))

+"""Plan de transport en base : services, arrêts desservis, OD et prix courants.
+
+Ces modèles ORM sont volontairement distincts des schémas Pydantic de l'API.
+"""
+
+from datetime import date
+from decimal import Decimal
+
+from sqlalchemy import (
+    CheckConstraint,
+    ForeignKey,
+    Numeric,
+    String,
+    UniqueConstraint,
+)
+from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column, relationship
+
+from cayzn.db import Base
+
+
+class Stop(Base):
+    """Lieu desservi, identifié par son code (ex. `ply` pour Paris Gare de Lyon)."""
+
+    __tablename__ = "stops"
+
+    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
+    code: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(16), unique=True)
+
+
+class Service(Base):
+    """Opération de transport (train, bus, vol), unique par nom et date de départ."""
+
+    __tablename__ = "services"
+    __table_args__ = (UniqueConstraint("name", "departure_date"),)
+
+    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
+    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(64))
+    departure_date: Mapped[date]
+
+    stops: Mapped[list[ServiceStop]] = relationship(
+        back_populates="service",
+        order_by="ServiceStop.position",
+        cascade="all, delete-orphan",
+    )
+    ods: Mapped[list[OriginDestination]] = relationship(
+        back_populates="service", cascade="all, delete-orphan"
+    )
+
+
+class ServiceStop(Base):
+    """Arrêt d'un service, à sa position dans l'itinéraire (0 = origine)."""
+
+    __tablename__ = "service_stops"
+    __table_args__ = (UniqueConstraint("service_id", "stop_id"),)
+
+    service_id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(
+        ForeignKey("services.id", ondelete="CASCADE"), primary_key=True
+    )
+    position: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
+    stop_id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(ForeignKey("stops.id"))
+
+    service: Mapped[Service] = relationship(back_populates="stops")
+    stop: Mapped[Stop] = relationship()
+
+
+class OriginDestination(Base):
+    """Trajet réservable entre deux arrêts d'un service, avec son prix courant."""
+
+    __tablename__ = "ods"
+    __table_args__ = (
+        UniqueConstraint("service_id", "origin_id", "destination_id"),
+        CheckConstraint("origin_id <> destination_id", name="distinct_stops"),
+        CheckConstraint("price >= 0", name="price_positive"),
+    )
+
+    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
+    service_id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(
+        ForeignKey("services.id", ondelete="CASCADE")
+    )
+    origin_id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(ForeignKey("stops.id"))
+    destination_id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(ForeignKey("stops.id"))
+    price: Mapped[Decimal | None] = mapped_column(Numeric(10, 2))
+
+    service: Mapped[Service] = relationship(back_populates="ods")
+    origin: Mapped[Stop] = relationship(foreign_keys=[origin_id])
+    destination: Mapped[Stop] = relationship(foreign_keys=[destination_id])

261	+if config.config_file_name is not None:
262	+    fileConfig(config.config_file_name)
263	+
264	+# % échappé : la config Alembic interpole les valeurs (mots de passe encodés).

275	+    """Run migrations in 'offline' mode.
276	+
277	+    This configures the context with just a URL
278	+    and not an Engine, though an Engine is acceptable
279	+    here as well.  By skipping the Engine creation
280	+    we don't even need a DBAPI to be available.
281	+
282	+    Calls to context.execute() here emit the given string to the
283	+    script output.
284	+
285	+    """
286	+    url = config.get_main_option("sqlalchemy.url")
287	+    context.configure(
288	+        url=url,
289	+        target_metadata=target_metadata,
290	+        render_as_batch=True,
291	+        literal_binds=True,
292	+        dialect_opts={"paramstyle": "named"},
293	+    )
294	+
295	+    with context.begin_transaction():
296	+        context.run_migrations()
297	+

300	+    """Run migrations in 'online' mode.
301	+
302	+    In this scenario we need to create an Engine
303	+    and associate a connection with the context.
304	+
305	+    """
306	+    connectable = engine_from_config(
307	+        config.get_section(config.config_ini_section, {}),
308	+        prefix="sqlalchemy.",
309	+        poolclass=pool.NullPool,
310	+    )
311	+
312	+    with connectable.connect() as connection:
313	+        context.configure(

561	+"""Import nocturne du plan de transport depuis les CSV du système de réservation.
562	+
563	+Usage : python -m cayzn.importer <dossier>  (trains.csv, stops.csv, ods.csv, prices.csv)
564	+
565	+L'import est idempotent : relancé sur les mêmes fichiers, il ne change rien.
566	+Tout est fait dans une seule transaction : une ligne invalide annule l'import entier.
567	+"""
568	+
569	+import csv
570	+import sys
571	+from collections.abc import Iterator
572	+from datetime import date
573	+from decimal import Decimal, InvalidOperation
574	+from pathlib import Path
575	+
576	+from sqlalchemy import select
577	+from sqlalchemy.orm import Session, selectinload
578	+
579	+from cayzn.db import SessionLocal
580	+from cayzn.models import OriginDestination, Service, ServiceStop, Stop
581	+
582	+ServiceKey = tuple[str, date]
583	+
584	+
585	+class TransportPlanError(ValueError):
586	+    pass
587	+
588	+
589	+def _rows(path: Path, columns: set[str]) -> Iterator[tuple[str, dict[str, str]]]:
590	+    """Lignes du CSV avec leur emplacement `fichier:ligne` pour les messages d'erreur."""
591	+    with path.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
592	+        reader = csv.DictReader(f)
593	+        missing = columns - set(reader.fieldnames or [])
594	+        if missing:
595	+            raise TransportPlanError(
596	+                f"{path.name}: colonnes manquantes {sorted(missing)}"
597	+            )
598	+        for row in reader:
599	+            where = f"{path.name}:{reader.line_num}"
600	+            if any(not (row[c] or "").strip() for c in columns):
601	+                raise TransportPlanError(f"{where}: valeur vide")
602	+            yield where, {c: row[c].strip() for c in columns}
603	+
604	+
605	+def _service_key(where: str, row: dict[str, str]) -> ServiceKey:
606	+    try:
607	+        return row["name"], date.fromisoformat(row["departure_date"])
608	+    except ValueError:
609	+        raise TransportPlanError(
610	+            f"{where}: date invalide {row['departure_date']!r}"
611	+        ) from None
612	+
613	+
614	+def import_transport_plan(session: Session, directory: Path) -> None:
615	+    keys = [
616	+        _service_key(where, row)
617	+        for where, row in _rows(directory / "trains.csv", {"departure_date", "name"})
618	+    ]
619	+
620	+    # Précharge l'existant pour éviter une requête par ligne.
621	+    existing = session.scalars(
622	+        select(Service)
623	+        .where(Service.departure_date.in_({d for _, d in keys}))
624	+        .options(selectinload(Service.stops), selectinload(Service.ods))
625	+    )
626	+    services: dict[ServiceKey, Service] = {
627	+        (s.name, s.departure_date): s for s in existing
628	+    }
629	+    for name, departure_date in keys:
630	+        if (name, departure_date) not in services:
631	+            services[name, departure_date] = Service(
632	+                name=name, departure_date=departure_date
633	+            )
634	+            session.add(services[name, departure_date])
635	+    services = {key: services[key] for key in keys}
636	+
637	+    stops = {s.code: s for s in session.scalars(select(Stop))}
638	+
639	+    def stop(code: str) -> Stop:
640	+        if code not in stops:
641	+            stops[code] = Stop(code=code)
642	+            session.add(stops[code])
643	+        return stops[code]
644	+
645	+    def service(where: str, row: dict[str, str]) -> Service:
646	+        key = _service_key(where, row)
647	+        if key not in services:
648	+            raise TransportPlanError(
649	+                f"{where}: service {key[0]} du {key[1]} absent de trains.csv"
650	+            )
651	+        return services[key]
652	+
653	+    # Itinéraires : l'ordre des lignes de stops.csv donne l'ordre de desserte.
654	+    itineraries: dict[ServiceKey, list[str]] = {}
655	+    for where, row in _rows(
656	+        directory / "stops.csv", {"departure_date", "name", "stops"}
657	+    ):
658	+        codes = itineraries.setdefault(_service_key(where, row), [])
659	+        service(where, row)
660	+        if row["stops"] in codes:
661	+            raise TransportPlanError(f"{where}: arrêt {row['stops']} en double")
662	+        codes.append(row["stops"])
663	+
664	+    for key, codes in itineraries.items():
665	+        svc = services[key]
666	+        if [s.stop.code for s in svc.stops] == codes:
667	+            continue
668	+        svc.stops.clear()
669	+        session.flush()  # supprime l'ancien itinéraire avant de réinsérer les mêmes clés
670	+        svc.stops.extend(
671	+            ServiceStop(position=i, stop=stop(c)) for i, c in enumerate(codes)
672	+        )
673	+
674	+    def od_key(od: OriginDestination) -> tuple[str, str]:
675	+        return od.origin.code, od.destination.code
676	+
677	+    ods = {(id(svc), *od_key(od)): od for svc in services.values() for od in svc.ods}
678	+
679	+    def find_od(
680	+        where: str, row: dict[str, str]
681	+    ) -> tuple[Service, OriginDestination | None]:
682	+        svc = service(where, row)
683	+        return svc, ods.get((id(svc), row["origin"], row["destination"]))
684	+
685	+    for where, row in _rows(
686	+        directory / "ods.csv", {"departure_date", "name", "origin", "destination"}
687	+    ):
688	+        svc, od = find_od(where, row)
689	+        if od:
690	+            continue
691	+        positions = {s.stop.code: s.position for s in svc.stops}
692	+        o, d = row["origin"], row["destination"]
693	+        if o not in positions or d not in positions:
694	+            raise TransportPlanError(
695	+                f"{where}: {o}-{d} n'est pas desservi par le service {svc.name}"
696	+            )
697	+        if positions[o] >= positions[d]:
698	+            raise TransportPlanError(
699	+                f"{where}: {o} n'est pas avant {d} dans l'itinéraire"
700	+            )
701	+        od = OriginDestination(origin=stop(o), destination=stop(d))
702	+        svc.ods.append(od)
703	+        ods[(id(svc), o, d)] = od
704	+
705	+    for where, row in _rows(
706	+        directory / "prices.csv",
707	+        {"departure_date", "name", "origin", "destination", "price"},
708	+    ):
709	+        _, od = find_od(where, row)
710	+        if od is None:
711	+            raise TransportPlanError(
712	+                f"{where}: OD {row['origin']}-{row['destination']} absente de ods.csv"
713	+            )
714	+        try:
715	+            price = Decimal(row["price"])
716	+        except InvalidOperation:
717	+            raise TransportPlanError(
718	+                f"{where}: prix invalide {row['price']!r}"
719	+            ) from None
720	+        if not price.is_finite() or price < 0:
721	+            raise TransportPlanError(f"{where}: prix invalide {row['price']!r}")
722	+        od.price = price
723	+
724	+
725	+if __name__ == "__main__":
726	+    if len(sys.argv) != 2:
727	+        sys.exit("usage: python -m cayzn.importer <dossier>")
728	+    with SessionLocal.begin() as session:
729	+        import_transport_plan(session, Path(sys.argv[1]))

738	+Ces modèles ORM sont volontairement distincts des schémas Pydantic de l'API.
739	+"""
740	+

+from logging.config import fileConfig
+
+from alembic import context
+from sqlalchemy import engine_from_config, pool
+
+from cayzn import models  # noqa: F401  (enregistre les tables)
+from cayzn.db import Base, settings
+
+# this is the Alembic Config object, which provides
+# access to the values within the .ini file in use.
+config = context.config
+
+# Interpret the config file for Python logging.
+# This line sets up loggers basically.
+if config.config_file_name is not None:
+    fileConfig(config.config_file_name)
+
+# % échappé : la config Alembic interpole les valeurs (mots de passe encodés).
+config.set_main_option("sqlalchemy.url", str(settings.database_url).replace("%", "%%"))
+target_metadata = Base.metadata
+
+# other values from the config, defined by the needs of env.py,
+# can be acquired:
+# my_important_option = config.get_main_option("my_important_option")
+# ... etc.
+
+
+def run_migrations_offline() -> None:
+    """Run migrations in 'offline' mode.
+
+    This configures the context with just a URL
+    and not an Engine, though an Engine is acceptable
+    here as well.  By skipping the Engine creation
+    we don't even need a DBAPI to be available.
+
+    Calls to context.execute() here emit the given string to the
+    script output.
+
+    """
+    url = config.get_main_option("sqlalchemy.url")
+    context.configure(
+        url=url,
+        target_metadata=target_metadata,
+        render_as_batch=True,
+        literal_binds=True,
+        dialect_opts={"paramstyle": "named"},
+    )
+
+    with context.begin_transaction():
+        context.run_migrations()
+
+
+def run_migrations_online() -> None:
+    """Run migrations in 'online' mode.
+
+    In this scenario we need to create an Engine
+    and associate a connection with the context.
+
+    """
+    connectable = engine_from_config(
+        config.get_section(config.config_ini_section, {}),
+        prefix="sqlalchemy.",
+        poolclass=pool.NullPool,
+    )
+
+    with connectable.connect() as connection:
+        context.configure(
+            connection=connection,
+            target_metadata=target_metadata,
+            render_as_batch=True,  # ALTER TABLE sous SQLite
+        )
+
+        with context.begin_transaction():
+            context.run_migrations()
+
+
+if context.is_offline_mode():
+    run_migrations_offline()
+else:
+    run_migrations_online()

+"""Import nocturne du plan de transport depuis les CSV du système de réservation.
+
+Usage : python -m cayzn.importer <dossier>  (trains.csv, stops.csv, ods.csv, prices.csv)
+
+L'import est idempotent : relancé sur les mêmes fichiers, il ne change rien.
+Tout est fait dans une seule transaction : une ligne invalide annule l'import entier.
+"""
+
+import csv
+import sys
+from collections.abc import Iterator
+from datetime import date
+from decimal import Decimal, InvalidOperation
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from sqlalchemy import select
+from sqlalchemy.orm import Session, selectinload
+
+from cayzn.db import SessionLocal
+from cayzn.models import OriginDestination, Service, ServiceStop, Stop
+
+ServiceKey = tuple[str, date]
+
+
+class TransportPlanError(ValueError):
+    pass
+
+
+def _rows(path: Path, columns: set[str]) -> Iterator[tuple[str, dict[str, str]]]:
+    """Lignes du CSV avec leur emplacement `fichier:ligne` pour les messages d'erreur."""
+    with path.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
+        reader = csv.DictReader(f)
+        missing = columns - set(reader.fieldnames or [])
+        if missing:
+            raise TransportPlanError(
+                f"{path.name}: colonnes manquantes {sorted(missing)}"
+            )
+        for row in reader:
+            where = f"{path.name}:{reader.line_num}"
+            if any(not (row[c] or "").strip() for c in columns):
+                raise TransportPlanError(f"{where}: valeur vide")
+            yield where, {c: row[c].strip() for c in columns}
+
+
+def _service_key(where: str, row: dict[str, str]) -> ServiceKey:
+    try:
+        return row["name"], date.fromisoformat(row["departure_date"])
+    except ValueError:
+        raise TransportPlanError(
+            f"{where}: date invalide {row['departure_date']!r}"
+        ) from None
+
+
+def import_transport_plan(session: Session, directory: Path) -> None:
+    keys = [
+        _service_key(where, row)
+        for where, row in _rows(directory / "trains.csv", {"departure_date", "name"})
+    ]
+
+    # Précharge l'existant pour éviter une requête par ligne.
+    existing = session.scalars(
+        select(Service)
+        .where(Service.departure_date.in_({d for _, d in keys}))
+        .options(selectinload(Service.stops), selectinload(Service.ods))
+    )
+    services: dict[ServiceKey, Service] = {
+        (s.name, s.departure_date): s for s in existing
+    }
+    for name, departure_date in keys:
+        if (name, departure_date) not in services:
+            services[name, departure_date] = Service(
+                name=name, departure_date=departure_date
+            )
+            session.add(services[name, departure_date])
+    services = {key: services[key] for key in keys}
+
+    stops = {s.code: s for s in session.scalars(select(Stop))}
+
+    def stop(code: str) -> Stop:
+        if code not in stops:
+            stops[code] = Stop(code=code)
+            session.add(stops[code])
+        return stops[code]
+
+    def service(where: str, row: dict[str, str]) -> Service:
+        key = _service_key(where, row)
+        if key not in services:
+            raise TransportPlanError(
+                f"{where}: service {key[0]} du {key[1]} absent de trains.csv"
+            )
+        return services[key]
+
+    # Itinéraires : l'ordre des lignes de stops.csv donne l'ordre de desserte.
+    itineraries: dict[ServiceKey, list[str]] = {}
+    for where, row in _rows(
+        directory / "stops.csv", {"departure_date", "name", "stops"}
+    ):
+        codes = itineraries.setdefault(_service_key(where, row), [])
+        service(where, row)
+        if row["stops"] in codes:
+            raise TransportPlanError(f"{where}: arrêt {row['stops']} en double")
+        codes.append(row["stops"])
+
+    for key, codes in itineraries.items():
+        svc = services[key]
+        if [s.stop.code for s in svc.stops] == codes:
+            continue
+        svc.stops.clear()
+        session.flush()  # supprime l'ancien itinéraire avant de réinsérer les mêmes clés
+        svc.stops.extend(
+            ServiceStop(position=i, stop=stop(c)) for i, c in enumerate(codes)
+        )
+
+    def od_key(od: OriginDestination) -> tuple[str, str]:
+        return od.origin.code, od.destination.code
+
+    ods = {(id(svc), *od_key(od)): od for svc in services.values() for od in svc.ods}
+
+    def find_od(
+        where: str, row: dict[str, str]
+    ) -> tuple[Service, OriginDestination | None]:
+        svc = service(where, row)
+        return svc, ods.get((id(svc), row["origin"], row["destination"]))
+
+    for where, row in _rows(
+        directory / "ods.csv", {"departure_date", "name", "origin", "destination"}
+    ):
+        svc, od = find_od(where, row)
+        if od:
+            continue
+        positions = {s.stop.code: s.position for s in svc.stops}
+        o, d = row["origin"], row["destination"]
+        if o not in positions or d not in positions:
+            raise TransportPlanError(
+                f"{where}: {o}-{d} n'est pas desservi par le service {svc.name}"
+            )
+        if positions[o] >= positions[d]:
+            raise TransportPlanError(
+                f"{where}: {o} n'est pas avant {d} dans l'itinéraire"
+            )
+        od = OriginDestination(origin=stop(o), destination=stop(d))
+        svc.ods.append(od)
+        ods[(id(svc), o, d)] = od
+
+    for where, row in _rows(
+        directory / "prices.csv",
+        {"departure_date", "name", "origin", "destination", "price"},
+    ):
+        _, od = find_od(where, row)
+        if od is None:
+            raise TransportPlanError(
+                f"{where}: OD {row['origin']}-{row['destination']} absente de ods.csv"
+            )
+        try:
+            price = Decimal(row["price"])
+        except InvalidOperation:
+            raise TransportPlanError(
+                f"{where}: prix invalide {row['price']!r}"
+            ) from None
+        if not price.is_finite() or price < 0:
+            raise TransportPlanError(f"{where}: prix invalide {row['price']!r}")
+        od.price = price
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    if len(sys.argv) != 2:
+        sys.exit("usage: python -m cayzn.importer <dossier>")
+    with SessionLocal.begin() as session:
+        import_transport_plan(session, Path(sys.argv[1]))

+"""Plan de transport en base : services, arrêts desservis, OD et prix courants.
+
+Ces modèles ORM sont volontairement distincts des schémas Pydantic de l'API.
+"""
+
+from datetime import date
+from decimal import Decimal
+
+from sqlalchemy import (
+    CheckConstraint,
+    ForeignKey,
+    Numeric,
+    String,
+    UniqueConstraint,
+)
+from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column, relationship
+
+from cayzn.db import Base
+
+
+class Stop(Base):
+    """Lieu desservi, identifié par son code (ex. `ply` pour Paris Gare de Lyon)."""
+
+    __tablename__ = "stops"
+
+    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
+    code: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(16), unique=True)
+
+
+class Service(Base):
+    """Opération de transport (train, bus, vol), unique par nom et date de départ."""
+
+    __tablename__ = "services"
+    __table_args__ = (UniqueConstraint("name", "departure_date"),)
+
+    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
+    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(64))
+    departure_date: Mapped[date]
+
+    stops: Mapped[list[ServiceStop]] = relationship(
+        back_populates="service",
+        order_by="ServiceStop.position",
+        cascade="all, delete-orphan",
+    )
+    ods: Mapped[list[OriginDestination]] = relationship(
+        back_populates="service", cascade="all, delete-orphan"
+    )
+
+
+class ServiceStop(Base):
+    """Arrêt d'un service, à sa position dans l'itinéraire (0 = origine)."""
+
+    __tablename__ = "service_stops"
+    __table_args__ = (UniqueConstraint("service_id", "stop_id"),)
+
+    service_id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(
+        ForeignKey("services.id", ondelete="CASCADE"), primary_key=True
+    )
+    position: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
+    stop_id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(ForeignKey("stops.id"))
+
+    service: Mapped[Service] = relationship(back_populates="stops")
+    stop: Mapped[Stop] = relationship()
+
+
+class OriginDestination(Base):
+    """Trajet réservable entre deux arrêts d'un service, avec son prix courant."""
+
+    __tablename__ = "ods"
+    __table_args__ = (
+        UniqueConstraint("service_id", "origin_id", "destination_id"),
+        CheckConstraint("origin_id <> destination_id", name="distinct_stops"),
+        CheckConstraint("price >= 0", name="price_positive"),
+    )
+
+    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
+    service_id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(
+        ForeignKey("services.id", ondelete="CASCADE")
+    )
+    origin_id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(ForeignKey("stops.id"))
+    destination_id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(ForeignKey("stops.id"))
+    price: Mapped[Decimal | None] = mapped_column(Numeric(10, 2))
+
+    service: Mapped[Service] = relationship(back_populates="ods")
+    origin: Mapped[Stop] = relationship(foreign_keys=[origin_id])
+    destination: Mapped[Stop] = relationship(foreign_keys=[destination_id])

+import shutil

+from pathlib import Path
+
+import pytest
+from sqlalchemy import create_engine, func, select

+
+from cayzn.db import Base
+from cayzn.importer import TransportPlanError, import_transport_plan
+from cayzn.models import OriginDestination, Service, ServiceStop, Stop
+
+FILES = Path(__file__).parents[1] / "files"
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def session():
+    engine = create_engine("sqlite://")
+    Base.metadata.create_all(engine)
+    with Session(engine) as session:
+        yield session
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def plan(tmp_path):
+    for f in FILES.glob("*.csv"):
+        shutil.copy(f, tmp_path)
+    return tmp_path
+
+
+def count(session, model):
+    return session.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(model))
+
+
+def itinerary(session, name):
+    service = session.scalars(select(Service).where(Service.name == name)).one()
+    return [s.stop.code for s in service.stops]
+
+
+def test_import_sample_files(session):
+    import_transport_plan(session, FILES)
+    session.commit()
+
+    assert count(session, Service) == 5
+    assert count(session, Stop) == 5
+    assert itinerary(session, "9410") == ["ply", "lpd", "msc"]
+    od = session.scalars(
+        select(OriginDestination)
+        .join(OriginDestination.service)
+        .where(Service.name == "9410", OriginDestination.price == Decimal(20))
+    ).one()
+    assert (od.origin.code, od.destination.code) == ("ply", "msc")
+
+
+def test_reimport_is_idempotent(session):
+    for _ in range(2):
+        import_transport_plan(session, FILES)
+        session.commit()
+
+    assert count(session, Service) == 5
+    assert count(session, ServiceStop) == 7

content.text:
# Revue des 4 derniers commits (`a74e461..HEAD`, hors transcripts)

Il n'y a aucune modification de code en attente, donc j'ai relu ce qui a été commité depuis `a74e461` : settings, modèles, migration Alembic, importer et justfile. Le seul problème sérieux touche l'importer. Je l'ai reproduit avec un script.

## 🔴 Important

**Après un changement d'itinéraire, `import_transport_plan` garde des OD invalides** (`src/cayzn/importer.py:664-703`)
Les OD existants ne sont jamais supprimés. Si un service ne dessert plus un arrêt, ou si l'ordre des arrêts change, ses anciens OD (avec leur prix) restent en base. L'importer refuserait pourtant ces mêmes OD dans un nouvel import. Reproduction : 9410 passe de `ply,lpd,msc` à `ply,msc`, et on ne garde que l'OD `ply-msc` dans `ods.csv` et `prices.csv`.
```
itinerary ['ply', 'msc']
ods [('ply','lpd',40.00), ('ply','msc',20.00), ('lpd','msc',50.00)]
```
Les 2 OD `ply-lpd` et `lpd-msc` sont toujours là. Le même défaut existe un cran plus loin : un OD absent de `ods.csv` n'est jamais supprimé, et un OD absent de `prices.csv` garde son ancien prix. Aucun test ne le voit, parce que `test_reimport_updates_itinerary_and_price` ne fait qu'ajouter un arrêt.
**Correctif minimal :** dans la boucle des itinéraires, quand `codes` change, retirer de `svc.ods` les OD dont l'origine ou la destination n'est plus dans `codes` ou n'est plus dans le bon ordre. `delete-orphan` s'occupe de la suppression en base.

## 🟡 Mineur

- **Prix hors limites** (`importer.py:714-722`) : la colonne est `Numeric(10, 2)`. Un prix comme `55.555` est arrondi sans prévenir, et un prix de plus de 8 chiffres avant la virgule fait planter Postgres avec une `DataError` brute au lieu d'une `TransportPlanError`. Il suffirait d'ajouter `price.as_tuple().exponent >= -2` et une borne max à la validation.
- **`.env.example:2`** renvoie à `compose.yaml`, mais le fichier versionné s'appelle `docker-compose.yaml`.
- **`justfile`, recette `test`** : `ENV=test` n'est lu nulle part, puisque `Settings` ne définit que `database_url`. On peut le retirer.
- **`justfile`, recette `pre-commit-install`** : `uv pip install pre-commit` installe hors du lock alors que pre-commit est déjà dans le groupe dev. `uv run pre-commit install` suffit.
- **`justfile`, recette `run`** : elle fait la même chose que `fastapi dev` dans le README. Garde l'une des deux.
- **`migrations/env.py:290,316`** : `render_as_batch=True` porte le commentaire « ALTER TABLE sous SQLite », alors que le projet n'accepte plus que Postgres (`PostgresDsn`). L'option est inutile.
- **README, lignes 18-19** : l'URL indiquée après `docker compose up -d` est exactement la valeur par défaut. `docker compose up -d` seul suffit.

## ✅ Ce qui est bien fait

- Tout l'import tient dans une transaction, les erreurs indiquent le `fichier:ligne`, et la validation se fait à l'entrée des CSV.
- Les contraintes sont aussi posées en base (CHECK, UNIQUE, FK avec CASCADE), et la `naming_convention` permet à Alembic de les retrouver.
- Les données existantes sont chargées en une seule requête, sans requête par ligne (pas de N+1).
- Les tests tournent sur SQLite en mémoire, sans Postgres.

Avant de corriger l'importer, une question : les CSV sont-ils un **instantané complet** du plan (tout ce qui manque doit être supprimé) ou un **delta** ? La réponse décide si on purge seulement les OD devenus invalides, ou tout ce qui n'apparaît plus dans les fichiers.

import shutil
from decimal import Decimal
from pathlib import Path

import pytest
from sqlalchemy import create_engine, func, select
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from cayzn.db import Base
from cayzn.importer import TransportPlanError, import_transport_plan
from cayzn.models import OriginDestination, Service, ServiceStop, Stop

FILES = Path(__file__).parents[1] / "files"


@pytest.fixture
def session():
    engine = create_engine("sqlite://")
    Base.metadata.create_all(engine)
    with Session(engine) as session:
        yield session


@pytest.fixture
def plan(tmp_path):
    for f in FILES.glob("*.csv"):
        shutil.copy(f, tmp_path)
    return tmp_path


def count(session, model):
    return session.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(model))


def itinerary(session, name):
    service = session.scalars(select(Service).where(Service.name == name)).one()
    return [s.stop.code for s in service.stops]


def test_import_sample_files(session):
    import_transport_plan(session, FILES)
    session.commit()

    assert count(session, Service) == 5
    assert count(session, Stop) == 5
    assert itinerary(session, "9410") == ["ply", "lpd", "msc"]
    od = session.scalars(
        select(OriginDestination)
        .join(OriginDestination.service)
        .where(Service.name == "9410", OriginDestination.price == Decimal(20))
    ).one()
    assert (od.origin.code, od.destination.code) == ("ply", "msc")


def test_reimport_is_idempotent(session):
    for _ in range(2):
        import_transport_plan(session, FILES)
        session.commit()

    assert count(session, Service) == 5
    assert count(session, ServiceStop) == 7
    assert count(session, OriginDestination) == 5


def test_reimport_updates_itinerary_and_price(session, plan):
    import_transport_plan(session, plan)
    session.commit()

    (plan / "stops.csv").write_text(
        "departure_date,name,stops\n2024-11-15,7866,ply\n2024-11-15,7866,lpd\n"
        "2024-11-15,7866,msc\n"
    )
    (plan / "ods.csv").write_text(
        "departure_date,name,origin,destination\n2024-11-15,7866,ply,msc\n"
    )
    (plan / "prices.csv").write_text(
        "departure_date,name,origin,destination,price\n2024-11-15,7866,ply,msc,55.5\n"
    )
    import_transport_plan(session, plan)
    session.commit()

    assert itinerary(session, "7866") == ["ply", "lpd", "msc"]
    assert itinerary(session, "9410") == ["ply", "lpd", "msc"]
    prices = session.scalars(
        select(OriginDestination.price)
        .join(OriginDestination.service)
        .where(Service.name == "7866")
    ).all()
    assert prices == [Decimal("55.50")]

def test_invalid_rows_are_rejected(session, plan, file, content, error):

L'importer refuse maintenant les prix que la colonne `Numeric(10, 2)` ne peut pas stocker tels quels, avec une `TransportPlanError` qui indique `fichier:ligne`. Les 13 tests passent, pre-commit aussi.

```python

        if (
            not price.is_finite()
            or not 0 <= price < 10**8
            or price != price.quantize(Decimal("0.01"))
        ):
```

Je n'ai pas repris le `exponent >= -2` que j'avais proposé en revue : il aurait refusé `55.500`, qui est pourtant un prix valide. Le code compare plutôt le prix à sa valeur arrondie au centime, ce qui refuse bien `55.555` mais accepte `55.500`. J'ai vérifié aussi que `55.50`, `99999999.99` et `0` passent.

Deux cas sont ajoutés à `test_invalid_rows_are_rejected` : `55.555` (trop de décimales) et `1e8` (trop grand).

Le problème le plus important de la revue n'est pas encore corrigé : les OD devenus invalides restent en base après un changement d'itinéraire. Pour le corriger, j'ai besoin de savoir si les CSV sont un instantané complet du plan ou un delta.

## Usage

To create a commit, just type:
```

Or with options:

6. If multiple distinct changes are detected, suggests breaking the commit into multiple smaller commits
